title: Secure C basics: bounds, input trust, format strings and resource handling
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify important assumptions and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a reviewed and tested exercise.

understand.concept: Secure C programming validates untrusted input, checks array and allocation bounds, uses correct format strings, manages resource lifetimes and avoids undefined behaviour. Format strings should normally be controlled by the program rather than supplied directly by untrusted input.
understand.whyItMatters: Memory safety and input validation defects can become security vulnerabilities. Security must be built into interfaces and error paths, not added only after functionality is complete.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.

explain.narrative:
Secure C programming validates untrusted input, checks array and allocation bounds, uses correct format strings, manages resource lifetimes and avoids undefined behaviour. Format strings should normally be controlled by the program rather than supplied directly by untrusted input.

State assumptions and constraints, consult the applicable standard or tool documentation, and verify the result with appropriate compiler diagnostics and tests. Separate portable guarantees from implementation-specific behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The format string is a trusted literal and the user-controlled text is supplied as a data argument. Passing user_text directly as the format string would allow percent sequences to be interpreted as directives.

practise.guidedTask: Explain the difference between printf("%s", text) and printf(text).
practise.independentTask: Review a C input routine for bounds, format-string, allocation and cleanup risks. Write a fix and regression tests.
hints: Use bounded input and validate conversion results.
Never pass untrusted text as a printf format string.
Keep ownership and cleanup paths explicit.
